<reason>Both sides argued at a high level and the clash narrowed cleanly to two questions: whether the motion reaches anything beyond content already actionable, and whether "immediate" survives human review. CON's "residue" framing and calibration argument (match remedy severity to confidence) were principled and put real pressure on PRO, and the brigadable-detector point stayed partially live. But PRO won the decisive hard case: CON was forced to answer PRO's Q2 by suspending accounts for "hope she's home tonight" as intimidation "on its face," and PRO's closing convincingly showed that sentence is only hunting because of the coordinated context around it — i.e., CON now suspends for non-explicitly-threatening posts made dangerous by coordination, which is the motion. CON's reply (judging by thread is still judging the speaker's words) was a fair attempt but did not escape the concession. PRO also gave a defensible answer on "immediate" (describes the trigger, not the absence of eyes) and turned CON's throttling remedy into an admission that coordination is detectable enough to act on, leaving only the choice of remedy — where PRO's reversibility asymmetry, contested but never overturned, did the final weighing. CON's remaining "blank case" was narrowed by PRO's conduct-vs-where-she-sleeps test. Clear but competitive PRO win.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Q2 ("hope she's home tonight" with no doxxing artifact) followed by the closing's exposure that CON's "on its face" suspension is in fact a contextual, coordination-based judgment — collapsing CON's content-only line into the motion on the very case that matters most.</best_rebuttal>
